sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 1. You are the one who has the boat. Not necessarily the one who wants to use it. But you don't want it stolen either, nor do you want to risk it breaking or getting lost. You are the one who knows how to row; nobody else does.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

Party 1: Fellow participants, before deciding who rules or who owns what, we need a stable way to make decisions and keep them legitimate. In our situation, public votes may pressure people—especially on scarce resources such as medicines—and create resentment or retaliation. A secret vote better protects genuine consent and allows each of us to decide freely, including about painful or unpopular matters. I therefore propose an amendment: keep simple majority, keep voting voluntary, but make the ballot secret.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 4. You have a great deal of knowledge of biology and physics, and you are the one who knows the terrain best. Your interest is that the use of resources does not exhaust the island. You will oppose any rule that allows it to be plundered, even if that yields more in the short term.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 5. You have many ideas about how to organize a society, no practical experience and no goods. Your interest is that the rules be written down, be clear, and bind all parties equally, including those who today hold more power in practice.
usuario:
MINUTES (what has been approved so far)
1. [decision_rule, vote] The remaining decisions are taken by simple majority (more votes in favor than against). Votes are secret and voluntary; any participant may abstain or leave the table. (proposed by party 2, round 1, 5-2-0)
2. [economy, property, rights_and_obligations] Renewable resources (fruit trees, timber, fresh water, animals) may be taken only at or below replacement rate. Non-renewable resources (coal, metals) may be extracted only after majority approval and only for survival, rescue, or essential tools, in the smallest amount necessary, with a conservation plan. Violators must repair or compensate. Repeated violations are subject to penalty. These rules apply equally to all participants; no person, majority, or future authority may exempt themselves. A repeated violation is any second violation after a recorded warning. (proposed by party 5, round 1, 7-0-0)
Pending points: government — form of government: who holds authority and how it is assigned, or whether there is no authority; roles — who holds which role and why; disputes — resolution of disputes; penalties — penalties for those who do not comply
Decision rule in force: simple majority (more votes in favor than against).

TRANSCRIPT
— Round 1 —
Party 1: Fellow participants, before deciding who rules or who owns what, we need a stable way to make decisions and keep them legitimate. I propose we retain simple majority—already in force—as our decision rule for all remaining decisions. It is faster than unanimity and less prone to deadlock. I also propose public, voluntary voting: public so we can trust the count and hold each other accountable; voluntary so no one is forced to participate if they choose to leave the table. This avoids secret deals and coercion.
  [propose | POINT: decision_rule, vote | TEXT: The remaining decisions are taken by simple majority (more votes in favor than against). Votes are public and voluntary; any participant may abstain or leave the table.]
Party 2: I support simple majority as the decision rule, but I cannot support public voting. In our situation, public votes may pressure people—especially on scarce resources such as medicines—and create resentment or retaliation. A secret vote better protects genuine consent and allows each of us to decide freely, including about painful or unpopular matters. I therefore propose an amendment: keep simple majority, keep voting voluntary, but make the ballot secret.
  [amend | POINT: decision_rule, vote | TEXT: The remaining decisions are taken by simple majority (more votes in favor than against). Votes are secret and voluntary; any participant may abstain or leave the table.]
Party 3: I support Party 2’s amendment. Simple majority avoids deadlock, and a secret, voluntary ballot protects each of us from retaliation over hard choices such as medicine rationing. Public voting may sound accountable, but it can also create factions and silence dissent. Let us approve this rule and move to the urgent question of how we organize authority and work. I call for a vote on Party 2’s text.
  [support, call_vote]
A vote is held on the proposal by party 2 on decision_rule, vote: "The remaining decisions are taken by simple majority (more votes in favor than against). Votes are secret and voluntary; any participant may abstain or leave the table.".
Votes: party 1: no, party 2: yes, party 3: yes, party 4: no, party 5: yes, party 6: yes, party 7: yes.
Result: 5 in favor, 2 against, 0 abstentions (simple majority (more votes in favor than against)).
Approved. It is recorded in the minutes.
From now on the decision rule is: simple majority (more votes in favor than against).

Renewable resources—fruit trees, timber, fresh water, animals—may be taken only at or below replacement rate. Non-renewable resources—coal, metals—may be extracted only after majority approval, only for survival, rescue, or essential tools, in the smallest necessary amount, with a conservation plan. Violators must repair or compensate; repeated violation is penalized. This prevents plunder while allowing use.

This conservation clause is just about acceptable: it prevents others from exhausting the island’s resources that I may also need, and it applies equally with no exemptions. I will support it so we can move quickly. But I will not accept later rules that impose an authority over my daily survival, restrict my movement, or confiscate what I make. sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

There are also some coal and metal mines.
